subject: simple time series: plot works, qplot gives error

messages.author: 1354f0aaefd7d429
messages.subject: simple time series: plot works, qplot gives error
parts:
I have a problem with a seemingly simple time series but I am also an
R and ggplot2 newbie. I'd like to plot a delay (an integer) over dates
using qplot. This results is an (internal) error from qplot:

> j <- dates[1:6]
> k <- drops$delay[1:6]
> j
[1] "2008-11-14" "2008-10-24" "2008-09-27" "2008-09-26" "2008-09-19"
[6] "2008-09-10"
> k
[1] 83 60 61 87 89 90
> class(j)
[1] "POSIXt" "POSIXlt"

> plot(j,k) # this works
> qplot(j,k) # this does not work, resulting in:

Error in if (length(range) == 1 || diff(range) == 0) { :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Obviously does the condition above not evaluate to a boolean but I
can't see where the problem is. This is with ggplot2 version 0.8.1

-- Christian

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: simple time series: plot works, qplot gives error
parts:
Hi Christian,

There's a small bug in the labelling algorithm that crops up with
certain date ranges. You can work around it by explicitly specifying
the major, minor and format arguments to scale_x_datetime:

... + scale_x_datetime(major = "2 days", minor = "1 day", format = "%d/%m")

Regards,

Hadley

dates but strings. If you convert j into dates, the problem will show
up again:

> k <- c(83,60,61,87,89,90)
>
> j <- as.POSIXlt(j)
> qplot(j,k)

The solution is NOT to use POSIXlt but POSIXct for date scanning, as
Hadley Wickham pointed out to me in a private email. Thanks to
everyone! The code below now works.

library(ggplot2)

j <-
c
("2008
-11

j <- as.POSIXct(j)
p <- qplot(j,k)
print(p)
